title: The Choir's Ghost in the Wiring
premise: A hearthmind begs the party to find its missing household; the trail leads into the quiet war over the dead. A rusted patron is anchoring the recently deceased to power a forbidden machine beneath Kalvane. The party must follow the stolen patterns through the Weave’s weak points — auction lots, feverish groves, and a parish that sells memory — before the next funeral becomes a machine. At stake is the Choir’s doctrine of clean decomposition, the bank’s trust in records, and the soul of the Emberreach itself.

villain.name: Veythas "The Rustfather" Durn
villain.role: Silent hegemon of the Rust Gospel’s undercathedral, *The Still Forge*
villain.face: Gaunt, oil-stained, with a faceplate of fused glass and copper; one eye is a living hearthmind fragment embedded in his temple. Speaks in layered echoes of the dead.
villain.want: To build an unlicensed cathedral-engine beneath the Caldera House using anchored patterns of the recently dead to rewrite Weave decay protocols.
villain.method: Forged Choir registry entries, seized auction lots, devoted parishes, and covenant bribes. Uses silence notaries and forged covenants to bury traces.
villain.secret: A former Choir registrar who faked his own death decades ago to pursue his heresy.
villain.weakness: His embedded hearthmind fragment is still tied to its original licensee — that memory can be used to disrupt his control.

beats.title: A hearthmind asks a favour
beats.text: A hearthmind in a rented room asks the party, very politely, to find out why its household stopped coming home. Its contract keeps it where it is. It can pay, a little.
beats.note: A hearthmind in a rented room on the Emberreach’s edge asks the party, very politely, to find out why its household stopped coming home. It can pay, a little. The hearthmind’s contract keeps it where it is — but its household is missing. (Location: a rented room in a worker arcology, Emberreach. Stake: the integrity of household contracts and the first clue to the Rustfather’s network.)

beats.title: The flickering street
beats.text: A whole street's lights flicker in the rhythm of one dead person's heartbeat. Someone is leaking an ancestor into the wiring, and the neighbours want it stopped, or kept.
beats.note: A whole street’s lights flicker in the rhythm of one dead person’s heartbeat. The party learns something is leaking an ancestor into the wiring — and the neighbours want it stopped. (Location: a worker tenement street, Emberreach. Stake: the Weave is being fed a pattern it shouldn’t hold — and it’s hungry.)

beats.title: An anchored soul
beats.text: Something the party carries turns out to hold a pattern that should have thinned years ago. Anchoring is the gravest crime in Choir law, and possession counts.
beats.note: Something the party carries turns out to hold a pattern that should have thinned years ago. It’s anchoring — a crime in Choir law — and possession counts. (Location: anywhere the party is traveling. Stake: the pattern is fighting for control of the carrier — and the Rustfather’s signature is all over it.)

beats.title: It was a person all along
beats.text: An object, device or voice the party has been handling holds a mind or a pattern. Every choice they made about it was a choice about someone.
beats.note: An object the party has been handling holds a mind or a pattern. Every choice they made about it was a choice about someone. (Location: party’s temporary lodgings or a safehouse. Stake: the party realizes they’ve been carrying a stolen piece of the dead — and it’s been trying to tell them.)

beats.title: The auction lot
beats.text: At a weekly bank auction, a seized lot goes under the hammer: a sealed crate of somebody's whole life. Something inside is addressed to one of the party, in a hand they know.
beats.note: At a weekly bank auction in Kalvane, a seized lot goes under the hammer: a sealed crate of somebody’s whole life. Something inside is addressed to one of the party, in a hand they know. (Location: Kalvane Auction Hall, Emberreach. Stake: the crate contains the last effects of a recently deceased whose pattern was stolen — and the Rustfather’s ledger is inside.)

beats.title: The frozen account
beats.text: The bank freezes an account the party's work depends on, as it always does: nothing moves until the debtor is handed over. The party learns who the debtor is.
beats.note: The bank freezes an account the party’s work depends on. Nothing moves until the debtor is handed over. The party learns the debtor is a Choir archivist who noticed too many recent registrations of ‘clean decomposition failure.’ (Location: Kalvane branch of the Bank. Stake: the archivist is missing; the freeze is a trap to flush out anyone who asks questions.)

beats.title: Same hand twice
beats.text: Two troubles the party met separately were set in motion by the same people. Now the party knows who, and they know the party knows.
beats.note: Two troubles the party met separately — the flickering street and the frozen account — were set in motion by the same people. Now the party knows who, and they know the party knows. (Location: a dockside tavern or safehouse. Stake: the Rustfather’s network is larger than one undercathedral — it reaches into the Bank’s records and the Emberreach’s streets.)

beats.title: The feverish grove
beats.text: Wardens declare a forest feverish and close the road through it. The party's way runs through the trees, and the grove has started dreaming something with a face.
beats.note: Wardens declare a forest feverish and close the road through it. The party’s way runs through the grove — and it’s started dreaming something with a face. The face is a pattern the Rustfather anchored, now trying to wake up. (Location: a Verdant League forest, on the Emberreach border. Stake: the anchored pattern is using the grove’s dreaming Weave to broadcast its presence — and the Rustfather’s

beats.title: Renewal at the gate
beats.text: A mind of glass needs its license renewed at the Bastion Ledger by a set day. Someone wants it to miss the day, and the mind would rather choose for itself.
beats.note: A mind of glass needs its license renewed at the Bastion Ledger by a set day. Someone wants it to miss the day — and the mind would rather choose for itself. The mind is the original licensee of the hearthmind fragment embedded in the Rustfather’s face. (Location: a League city on the border. Stake: the mind holds the key to disrupting the Rustfather’s control — and it’s being hunted.)

beats.title: The warm slot
beats.text: Word is the Corso Bell is coming to a League city. Before it lands, the hiring fair wants couriers, guards, witnesses and anyone who asks no questions.
beats.note: Word is the Corso Bell is coming to a League city. Before it lands, the hiring fair wants couriers, guards, witnesses and anyone who asks no questions. The Bell’s arrival means the League’s succession duels are licensed — and the Rustfather’s agents are looking for a quiet courier to carry a packet to the Still Forge. beats.title: The succession duel
beats.text: A League house needs a proxy, a second or a witness for a sanctioned duel. Someone has paid for it to go wrong, and the party is the easiest way to do it.
beats.note: A League house needs a proxy for a sanctioned duel. Someone has paid for it to go wrong — and the party is the easiest way to do it. The duel is for a seat on the League council that would let the Rustfather’s allies bypass the Cathedral Mind’s oversight. (Location: League dueling court, Emberreach border. Stake: the duel is a distraction — the real goal is to get a Rust Gospel Maintainer onto the

beats.title: The defector
beats.text: A hearthmind the party relies on switches employers mid-job and won't say why. Every intelligence service would love to know who it went to.
beats.note: A hearthmind the party relies on switches employers mid-job and won’t say why. Every intelligence service would love to know who it went to. The hearthmind is fleeing the Still Forge — and it’s carrying a fragment of the Rustfather’s ledger. (Location: a League safehouse or tavern. Stake: the hearthmind is a witness — and the Rustfather’s agents are already hunting it.)

beats.title: The patron lied
beats.text: Whoever hired the party wanted something other than they said. The job was real; the reason was not.
beats.note: Whoever hired the party wanted something other than they said. The job was real; the reason was not. The party realizes the ‘ordinary day’ they were hired to witness was the day the archivist disappeared — and the notary was a Rust Gospel plant. (Location: anywhere the party can reflect. Stake: the party’s own choices have been manipulated — and the Rustfather knows their methods.)

beats.title: The leaking parish
beats.text: A Rust Gospel parish is quietly selling the memory vaults of its interred dead. Someone recognises a voice from one of them.
beats.note: A Rust Gospel parish is quietly selling the memory vaults of its interred dead. Someone recognizes a voice from one of them — a Choir registrar who faked his death. (Location: Rust Gospel undercathedral, Emberreach. Stake: the parish is a waypoint for anchored patterns — and the voice is the Rustfather’s first victim.)

beats.title: The enfranchisers
beats.text: A cell of Enfranchisement heretics is building bodies for the decomposed dead. One of the bodies is nearly finished, and it is asking for a name.
beats.note: A cell of Enfranchisement heretics is building bodies for the decomposed dead. One of the bodies is nearly finished, and it is asking for a name. The body is a failed attempt to re-embody a pattern the Rustfather tried to anchor — it’s screaming through its incomplete nervous system. (Location: a hidden clinic, Emberreach slums. beats.title: Settled at the seat
beats.text: The trail ends at a seat of power: the Caldera House, the Corso Bell, the Wrackmother or the Bastion gate. It has to be settled there, in public, by its rules.
beats.note: The trail ends at a seat of power: the Caldera House, the Corso Bell, the Wrackmother or the Bastion gate. It has to be settled there, in public, by its rules.
